_README: Measured model metrics. Regenerated by backend/ml/train_clean_corpus.py on
every retrain and served by GET /api/v1/model/performance. Never hand-edit
recall numbers: they are the output of the scripts named in 'sources'.
All holdout preprocessing uses the saved scaler pipeline + training imputer

weighting.note: v1 applied MULTICLASS inverse-frequency weights to BOTH models. v2 uses per-target weights, capped.

headline_verdict.summary: At matched false-positive rates the retrained models do not discriminate better than the existing ones. The weight fix is a correctness fix that recalibrates the score scale; it does not raise separation quality.
headline_verdict.evidence: At C2 FPR ~4%: v1@T=0.70 gives IDS2025 attack recall 52.45%, v2@T=0.25 gives 50.83%. At C2 FPR ~0.25%: v1@T=0.90 gives 45.93%, v2@T=0.45 gives 45.47%.

holdouts.C1_session_split: friday_ddos_test + friday_bot_test — 39,918 rows, zero training overlap
holdouts.C2_temporal_benign: friday_benign_c2 — 286,785 BENIGN rows, never in training
holdouts.ids2025_validation: ids2025_validation.csv — 91,830 rows, cross-source (26,185 BENIGN / 65,645 attack; 36,267 rows carry labels absent from training)

threshold_sweeps._note: Each row is a raw P(attack) cut. Read the FPR column together with recall; the fixed-T comparison below is misleading on its own.

tier1_at_deployed_cut_percent_RETRACTED.why_retracted: Measured before the Fwd-Header-Length rename fix. On that path every Friday-derived row (Bot rows included) had a canonical column nulled and median-imputed, which shifted the whole score distribution up by roughly +0.3; the same defect produced the 18.24%/6.79% C2 FPR pair later traced and corrected in documentation_discrepancy. The canonical-path value is the 59.82% above.

bot.finding: The 65-68% figure was the Tier-1 multiclass label only, and the binary gate's true held-out Bot recall at the deployed cut is 59.82% (not 99.47% - see tier1_at_deployed_cut_percent_RETRACTED). The Tier-2 rf_bot_binary specialist then accepts 100% of the Bot flows the gate passes, so the gate is the binding constraint and the end-to-end Bot recall is simply the gate's. The specialist's own 95.56% precision / 100% recall figure was measured on the streamed corpus at P(Bot|flagged)=0.0222 with no gate in front of it; on friday_bot_test + the C2 BENIGN holdout (287,355 rows, P(Bot)=0.0020) its 0.50 cut scores 64.67% precision / 60.70% recall standalone.
bot.caution: A gate and its cut are not interchangeable across retrains. v3 at v1's 0.65 cut flags 0.16% of the clean BENIGN holdout and passes 0 of 570 held-out Bot flows to the specialist (0.0% end-to-end). Always pair a gate with the cut calibrated for it - backend/realtime/thresholds.json.

infiltration.true_provenance: 20/29 rows on the IDS2025 validation set — statistically meaningless.
infiltration.finding: Cannot be validly evaluated with the data present: the only cross-dataset Infiltration holdout has 36 rows and the IDS2025 one has 29. A new dedicated Infiltration specialist scored 19.4% recall against the Tier-1 model's 77.8% on those 36 rows and is NOT recommended for promotion.
infiltration.recommendation: Build a proper held-out split from the 161,934 CICIDS2018 Infiltration rows before claiming anything about this class.

false_infiltration_labels_dominate_resid.measured_on_streamed_corpus: at T=0.65, 980 of 986 flows labelled Infiltration were truly BENIGN — 76% of all remaining false positives
false_infiltration_labels_dominate_resid.implication: Improving Infiltration precision matters more than improving its recall.

deployment_recommendation.reason: v2 had no discrimination gain at matched FPR and lost Bot entirely at T=0.65. v3 is different: at the deployed false-positive budget (3.65% C2 BENIGN FPR, where v1's shipped T=0.65 sits) it is level with v1 on end-to-end Bot recall (60.18% vs 60.00%) and on C1 DDoS (99.9% both) while lifting cross-environment DDoS recall on the uncontaminated CIC-DDoS2019 probe from 12.52% to 51.43% (ROC-AUC 0.4916 -> 0.7025). THE CUT MUST MOVE WITH THE MODEL: v3 at 0.65 detects 0 of 570 held-out Bot flows.
deployment_recommendation.rollback: THREVIA_MODELS_DIR=hdfs://namenode:8020/threvia/models_clean plus ML_THRESHOLD=0.65 (or a v1 thresholds.json). The v1 gate still wins at strict operating points - see tier2_bot_behind_gate.roc_crossing.
deployment_recommendation.remaining_weakness: At C2 FPR <= 2% v1 dominates v3 on both axes (Bot 56.3/57.9/59.3% vs 24.4/27.5/31.1%; CIC-DDoS2019 DDoS 3.21/4.65/6.17% vs 1.90/2.12/3.30%). The promotion is justified only at the deployed 3.65% budget, not at a tighter one.

_README: Does v3 keep Bot detection alive once the Tier-2 specialist is measured BEHIND the gate?
The specialist is only consulted for flows the Tier-1 binary gate already
flagged, so end-to-end Bot recall = gate recall x specialist acceptance, and a
gate that misses Bot flows loses them before the specialist is asked.
all at matched C2 BENIGN false-positive rate. Every number measured.

supports.ddos2019_test: 306,201 (254,797 attack / 51,404 BENIGN), 0.000% fingerprint overlap with training
supports.note: friday_bot_test is a row-level randomSplit of the Friday Bot capture, so near-duplicate flows straddle it; treat its recall as an upper bound, as eval_bot_heldout.py does.

at_matched_c2_fpr._note: v1's matched cut for its own deployed FPR budget comes out at T=0.649 against a shipped T=0.65 - the method reproduces the live operating point, which is the check that the comparison is anchored where the pipeline actually runs.

tier2_bot_behind_gate.roc_crossing: v3's advantage is not a blanket improvement: the two ROCs cross near 3% C2 FPR. Below it v1 wins on BOTH end-to-end Bot and cross-environment DDoS; above it v3 wins both. The deployed v1 cut (0.65) sits at 3.65% C2 FPR, i.e. just past the crossing - so the promotion is conditional on the budget, not unconditional.

bot_specialist_standalone_on_the_hard_ho.holdout: friday_bot_test (570 Bot) + friday_benign_c2 (286,785 BENIGN) = 287,355 rows, P(Bot)=0.0020
bot_specialist_standalone_on_the_hard_ho.finding: The specialist never rejects a Bot flow the gate passes, so it adds no Bot recall of its own; its only live effect is the 189 BENIGN flows it relabels as Bot.

at_the_deployed_cut_0_65_raw.finding: This is the trap the promotion had to avoid: the raw cut is not portable between gates.

calibration_of_the_promoted_gate.why_severity_was_re_derived: Severity is read off P(attack), so a rescaled gate silently empties the Critical/High buckets the dashboard counts. Each step is anchored to a fraction of the tolerated benign rate (F, F/2, F/10) so the ladder stays comparable across gates.

deployed_pipeline_on_the_replay_corpus._note: Same method, same input (corpus/demo_balanced_150k_fixed, 113,928 flows: 75,000 BENIGN / 37,500 DDoS / 1,428 Bot), one gate and cut per row. Script: backend/ml/measure_stream_fpr.py (logs /tmp/stream_fpr_v1.log, /tmp/stream_fpr_v3.log).
deployed_pipeline_on_the_replay_corpus.reading: On this synthetic, CIC-2017-derived balanced replay the promotion is mildly negative on its own terms: +694 benign false positives (+0.92 pp FPR), recall unchanged (98.53% vs 98.56%), precision -1.57 pp. The benefit v3 buys is invisible here by construction - this corpus comes from the same capture environment the v1 models were trained on - and shows up only on the cross-environment probe (CIC-DDoS2019 DDoS recall 12.52% -> 51.43% at matched C2 FPR). Bot is essentially unchanged (gate pass 63.4% -> 61.6%).
deployed_pipeline_on_the_replay_corpus.why_the_anchors_differ: The cut is matched on the clean C2 temporal holdout (3.73% there), which lands at 4.15% on the replay corpus because the replay corpus has a different, synthetic BENIGN mix. Matching on the replay corpus instead would need T~=0.35, which on C1 puts v3's Bot gate recall on a cliff (31.75% at T=0.40, 59.30% at T=0.315) and buys nothing the C2 anchor does not already justify.
deployed_pipeline_on_the_replay_corpus.cross_check: The v1 row independently reproduces two numbers published elsewhere: the streamed-corpus 3.26% FPR at T=0.65 (measured here as 3.23%) and P(Bot|flagged)=0.0222 from detection_policy.py (measured here as 0.0222).

documentation_discrepancy.root_cause: The 18.24%/6.79% figures previously reported here as 'the reproducible values' were themselves the artifact. The evaluation sweep scripts pre-selected columns before cleaning, so rows missing the canonical 'Fwd Header Length' (all Friday parquets carry only the FwdHeaderLength34/55 duplicates) were silently null'd and median-imputed, making benign rows look like median-FHL attack training rows. With the rename applied (now fixed inside clean_and_scale_external's callers), v1 reproduces the documented table exactly.
documentation_discrepancy.action: The documented 12.87%/3.65% figures are the faithful ones. Earlier claims of non-reproducibility in this artifact and in the Sept-17 doc section are retracted.

infiltration_split_evaluation.split: Temporal 50/50 split of the 161,934 CICIDS2018 Infiltration rows (boundary = median timestamp; no source-IP column exists, so session grouping is impossible). Test side de-leaked on canonical-feature hash: 4,558 of 72,022 test rows shared a hash with the train side and were removed.
infiltration_split_evaluation.deployed_v1_models_note: v1 trained on ALL Infiltration rows, so 99.97% Tier-1 recall on the test side is IN-SAMPLE (upper bound), not a generalisation claim.

specialist_split_aware_leak_free.note: First leak-free Infiltration measurement in the project. Same-source temporal holdout; near-perfect recall reflects that Infiltration flows are highly distinctive within their own source, NOT cross-source skill. Cross-dataset generalisation remains unproven (see the 36-row CIC-2017 check).

cross_dataset_generalization_check_36_ro.status: demoted to secondary evidence; supports too small to separate detectors

production_mitigation.action: Infiltration-label suppression routed to manual_review collection
production_mitigation.justification: 980/986 Infiltration-labelled streamed flows were truly BENIGN (76% of residual FPs); 7.44% BENIGN FPR confirmed on C2 holdout (21,342/286,785)
production_mitigation.config: SUPPRESS_INFILTRATION=false to disable; on by default

_README: Step-1 DATA audit plus a data-selection retrain (models_clean_v3).
backend/ml/compare_at_matched_fpr.py. Every number below is measured.

duplicates.largest_group_labels: FTP-Patator=85,926 and DoS Slowhttptest=46,512 share ONE identical 78-feature vector
duplicates.finding: The corpus contains rows that are bit-identical but labelled differently. No classifier can separate them. This is the mechanical cause of the long-standing 'DoS Slowhttptest is ~55% misclassified as FTP-Patator' symptom, and it is irreducible error, not a model defect.

source_monopoly.finding: Seven of fourteen classes were trained on LycoS and ONLY LycoS (measured via the 5 canonical columns LycoS lacks: rows sitting on the imputed median).

unused_datasets_in_data_folder.new_dos: CIC-DDoS2019, 431,371 rows, SAME CICFlowMeter schema (mappable) - but its parquet exports have no Destination Port, so it is used as a HOLDOUT only, never as training data
unused_datasets_in_data_folder.verdict: CTU-13 and UNSW-NB15 CANNOT be merged into this model at all - they do not share the 78-feature CICFlowMeter schema and would need a separate feature pipeline and a separate model. That is the answer to 'did I pick the wrong datasets': two of the three, yes, but they were never usable here in the first place.

unused_compatible_data_that_was_simply_n.what: CIC-2017 Tuesday (FTP/SSH-Patator), Wednesday (DoS Hulk/GoldenEye/slowloris/Slowhttptest), Thursday (Web Attacks, Infiltration)
unused_compatible_data_that_was_simply_n.note: The Friday files are deliberately excluded because the C1 holdout (friday_ddos_test, friday_bot_test) and the port-grouped PortScan holdout are split out of them.

holdout_contamination_finding.ids2025: NOT a cross-source set. 86.9% of its PortScan rows, 63.9% of its Bot rows, and - after the v3 CIC-2017 additions - 75.9% of its DoS/DDoS rows and 53.0% of its Brute Force rows are the SAME PHYSICAL FLOWS as the training data (exact fingerprint match on 16 encoding-stable canonical columns).
holdout_contamination_finding.action: IDS2025 must stop being used as a generalisation probe. Its apparent v3 gains (Brute Force 0.12% -> 82.84%) are leakage, NOT improvement.
holdout_contamination_finding.clean_replacement: corpus/ddos2019_test - CIC-DDoS2019's own testing split, 306,201 rows (254,797 DDoS / 51,404 BENIGN). Measured 0.000% fingerprint overlap against corpus/train, cic17_extra and the Friday splits.
holdout_contamination_finding.friday_c2_is_sound: 0 of 286,785 C2 BENIGN rows appear in benign_train, so the temporal C2 FPR anchor is trustworthy.

data_bug_fixed_label_encoding.what: All 2,180 CIC-2017 Thursday Web Attack rows were being silently dropped.
data_bug_fixed_label_encoding.cause: The label separator is the UTF-8 replacement character U+FFFD (bytes EF BF BD) - an earlier spreadsheet round-trip destroyed the en-dash. The LABEL_NORMALISE entries written as 'WEB ATTACK \x96 ...' can never match that, and no reader encoding recovers it (Latin-1 only turns one bad character into three).
data_bug_fixed_label_encoding.fix: schema_maps.label_lookup_key() collapses every non-ASCII character to '-', so those labels land on the existing ASCII 'WEB ATTACK - ...' keys. Verified: Web Attack rows merged went 0 -> 2,180.

v3_training.relation_to_v2: v3 keeps v2's corrected per-target capped weights; the only change is the added CIC-2017 attack sources.

clean_cross_environment_result.interpretation: The deployed v1 model is at CHANCE (AUC 0.49) at telling new-environment DDoS from new-environment BENIGN. v3 lifts that to 0.70. This is the one uncontaminated demonstration that the data-selection repair improved real generalisation.

regression.finding: v3 trades Tier-1 Bot recall for cross-environment DDoS discrimination. Bot is nominally covered by the Tier-2 rf_bot_binary specialist, so this must be re-measured on the v3 gate before switching models.
regression.resolved_by_tier2_bot_behind_gate: Measured (see tier2_bot_behind_gate). At the deployed false-positive budget the trade is a tie on Bot (60.18% vs 60.00% end-to-end) and a 4x win on cross-environment DDoS (51.43% vs 12.52%), but only once v3's cut is re-derived to 0.2575. At strict cuts (<=2% C2 FPR) v1 still wins on both.

deployment_recommendation_v3.reason: The data repairs are unambiguously correct (label sanitization recovering 2,180 rows; retiring the contaminated IDS2025 probe; the DDOS19 column map; the one-aggregation null imputation that removed ~78 redundant Spark jobs per dataset). The v3 MODEL fixes genuine new-environment DDoS blindness (AUC 0.49 -> 0.70). The follow-up this field asked for - re-measuring the Tier-2 Bot specialist behind the v3 gate - is done: at the deployed false-positive budget v3 is level with v1 on end-to-end Bot recall (60.18% vs 60.00%) and 4x better on cross-environment DDoS (51.43% vs 12.52%). PROMOTED with the cut re-derived to 0.2575 (backend/realtime/thresholds.json); v3 at the old 0.65 cut detects zero Bot.
deployment_recommendation_v3.hardware_note: The de-noised corpus rewrite (dropping the 20.8% duplicate rows and down-sampling DoS Hulk) is implemented behind REBUILD_CORPUS=1 in build_corpus_v3.py but cannot complete on this container: a 15.7M-row wide-frame shuffle exceeds its 7.6 GiB cap and is silently OOM-killed (exit 137). Run it with more container memory.
deployment_recommendation_v3.also: These evaluations must run with --master spark://spark-master:7077. In local[*] mode the driver shares the master container's 7.6 GiB with the user's long-running realtime simulation and gets OOM-killed.
